 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- for the death of Sri. SCCH 15 3 MVC No.5433/2023 Murugesh.N, S/o D.Nilakantashetty in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 16.07.2023 at about 07.30 a.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Sri. Murugesh.N was riding his Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-R-9279 on the left side of the HMT, main road, opposite, I.I.SC quarters, Yeshwanthapura,
Bangalore City, at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-04-HY-0909 ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and dashed to the scooter of the deceased Murugesh.
Due to impact, said Murugesh had sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after accident, Murugesh.N was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
But, during the course of treatment, he was succumbed to the injuries on 18.07.2023.
Thereafter the postmortem was conducted in the said hospital.
The Petitioners had spent about Rs.2,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequious SCCH 15 4 MVC No.5433/2023 ceremonies and Rs.20,000/- towards transportation of dead body.

Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a security guard in Tata Institute, Yeshwanthapura, Bangalore and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY-0909.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

Pankaja .M vs Shivam Dogoria on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132372356/
2 3.
In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, both Respondents appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and the Respondent No.2 filed its detailed Objection Statement.
The Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5433/2023 age,
avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending motor cycle by its rider and also the death of the Murugesh.N due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Further it denied that the issuance of policy in respect of offending motor cycle.
Further it contended that the vehicle was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1)Whether the Petitioners prove that Murugesh N. S/o D. Nilakantashetty was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 16.07.2023 at about 7.30 a.m., Opposite II Sc Quarters, HMT main road, Yeshwanthapura, Bengaluru, due to SCCH 15 6 MVC No.5433/2023 the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY- 0909??
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Murugesh N.?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

4) What Order or Award ?
5.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 23 documents at Ex.P.1 to 23 and closed her side evidence.
Further, she has examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 5 documents at Ex.P24 to 28 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

6. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5433/2023 perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 :
As per the Final Order for the following :

3
7. Issue No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioners that the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Murugesh.N was died in the road traffic accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY-0909.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5433/2023 No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P23.

Ex.P-1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the son of the deceased by name Rahul.M S/o Murugeshan.N, the Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY-0909 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P3 is the Requisition .
Ex.P.4 are the copy of Spot Mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P5 & 6 are the Police Intimations.
Ex.P7 & 8 are the Police Notice with Reply.
Ex.P9 is the Confessional Statement of the accused rider.
Ex.P10 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P11 is the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.5433/2023 Inquest Mahazar of the deceased.
Ex.P12 is the copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to coma as a result of head injury sustained.

Ex.P-13 is the true copy of the Charge-Sheet which shows that the I.O of the Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Car for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex . P14
is the In Patient Summary.
Ex . P15
and 16
are the Appointment order and Identity card of the deceased.
Ex.P17 is the Death Certificate of the deceased ie., Murugesh.
N. Ex.P18 to 21 are the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners and deceased.
Ex. P22
and 23
are the Bank Pass book of the Deceased.
11. P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.
Hence, it failed to substantiate its Objection statement contentions.
The Charge-sheet clearly shows that SCCH 15 10 MVC No.5433/2023 after investigation I.O has filed Charge-sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The Spot sketch also clearly shows that the offending vehicle came to right side and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioners and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that PW.1 has proved rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle by its rider and thereby the accident has occurred and in the said accident her husband was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."
12. Issue No.2 and 3:
Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.

4 13.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
Petitioner No.2 & 3 are children of the deceased Murugesh.N.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5433/2023 Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1 to 3 and deceased at Ex.P.18 to 21.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
14. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 50 years and deceased was working as Security Guard and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

In this regard, PW.1 has examined Administrative Officer of the M/s Cosmopolitan Industrial Security and Detective Services Pvt Ltd.,
by name Thippeswamy as PW.2 and he produced Attendance Register, Salary Statement, Pay Slips from March 2023 to July 2023 at Ex.P24 to 28.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Upon going through the Ex.P27 i.e., Pay Slip for the month of July 2023 of the deceased which shows the Gross salary is Rs.13,511/-.
The accident has occurred on 16.07.2023.
The Bank Passbook i.e., Ex.P22 shows the credit of salary of the deceased.
The Salary Statement of July 2023 shows the last salary drawn is Rs.11,896/-.
Hence, the salary of the deceased to be taken at Rs.13,511/-.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Murugesh was 50 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.21 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Murugesh.N which shows his date of birth was 27.11.1973.
The alleged accident has been occurred on 16.07.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Murugesh.N was 49 years, 07 months and 20 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Murugesh.N to be taken at 50 years for the purpose of assessment.
16. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
17.
The deceased has left behind him his wife and children.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 and SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5433/2023 3 are the son and daughter.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

Pankaja .M vs Shivam Dogoria on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132372356/
5 18.

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife and children of the deceased Murugesh.N, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards SCCH 15 14 MVC No.5433/2023 loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
19.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and daughter and they lost their father's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
20. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.5433/2023 VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:

21. It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was at Rs.13,511/- pm.
22.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "
- Held : - yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5433/2023 Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s SCCH 15 17 MVC No.5433/2023 Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 10% when the age is between 50 to 60 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 50 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 10% of the income has to be added.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.14,862/- p.m. (Rs.13,511/- + Rs.1351/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 13.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

23. After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.14,862/- it comes to Rs.9,908/-
(Rs.14,862/- - 4,954/-) and multiplier applied is 13 which comes to Rs.15,45,648/-
SCCH 15 18 MVC No.5433/2023 (Rs.9,908/- x 12 x 13).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,45,648/- towards loss of dependency.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
24 . The PW.1 has stated in her evidence that, she had spent huge amount towards medical treatment.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced medical bills at Ex.P14.
I have gone through the same.
The medical bill at Sl.No.1 shows total amount of Rs.3,58,337/-.
But, the advance paid Rs.2,05,000/-, the settlement discount at Rs.18,336.86/- and settled amount is Rs.1,35,000/-.
The Petitioner has produced the breakup bill which shows the balance due is Rs.1,53,337/-.
The Petitioner has produced advance receipts which shows about the payment of Rs.2,05,000/-.
The Petitioner has not produced any payment receipts towards the balance due of Rs.1,53,337/-.

Hence,
I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,05,000/- under this head.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of Consortium Rs. 1,45,200/-
(48,400X3)

3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/-
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/-
of dead body 6.

Medical expenses Rs. 2,05,000/-
7. Loss of Dependency Rs.15,45,648/-
Total Rs.19,87,148/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are awarded compensation of Rs.19,87,148/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

26. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the SCCH 15 20 MVC No.5433/2023 conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the negligent on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY-0909.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner No.1 to 3.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,87,148/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
 SCCH 15 21 MVC No.5433/2023  ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.19,87,148/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

8
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 60% to the Petitioner No.1.
SCCH 15 22 MVC No.5433/2023 After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 respectively by way of E-payment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 to 3 respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
